correctness.rationale: For the finite unit-edge cycle, KR duality identifies the attained sharp Lipschitz seminorm with W1 of neighboring heat rows, and an edge-circulation argument gives min_c sum_j|p_t(j)-c|. The radial difference system for q_d=p_t(d) is irreducible cooperative: q_0>q_1>...>q_floor(n/2) for every t>0. Counting multiplicities of radial entries gives the four exact median expressions for n=4r+a. Taylor expansion e^{-tL} shows p_t(d)=t^d/d!+O(t^(d+1)) before the antipode; plugging the four cuts yields contraction deficit b_a t^k/k! at k=floor((n+2)/4), b=(2,1,4,3). Spectral Fourier modes ±1 give leading e^{-4sin²(pi/n)t} and explicit trigonometric median sum c_n; remaining modes decay at λ_2 for n>=7. Boundary t=0 and all residue classes covered. Independent exact combinatorial leading coefficient check across 33 n agreed; experiments do not establish the universal limit.
residual_risks: Finite diagnostics are only corroboration; infinite assertions rest on the reconstructed proof.

value.rationale: Sharp contractivity of graph heat on finite cycles is a natural diffusion/transport invariant. The quarter-cycle delay to the first nonzero Taylor derivative is a meaningful high-order boundary phenomenon, and the all-time exact four-residue formula plus explicit long-time constants give quantitative information not supplied by standard generic curvature estimates. This is valuable even though circular flow duality and Fourier diagonalization are well known.
